tagline: An Ohio River road through Augusta carries Mary Draper Ingles’s name
intro: KY 8 follows the Ohio River through northern Kentucky, becoming Fifth Street in Augusta on the river’s south bank. The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet identifies the scenic Mary Ingles Highway as KY 8 through Augusta, designated November 24, 2008. At the waterfront, houses in the Water Street Historic District overlook the Ohio, with Victorian villas interspersed among earlier homes.

The highway’s name commemorates Mary Draper Ingles, captured by Shawnee in the summer of 1755 and taken to Lower Shawneetown at the Ohio and Scioto rivers. Later taken to Big Bone Lick to make salt, she escaped with another captive woman and followed the Ohio, Kanawha and New rivers toward Virginia. Her son John Ingles recorded her story in 1824, drawing on what he had heard from his parents.

Approaching Augusta from the northwest on KY 8, the drive reaches the river town that Philip Buckner founded as a trading post in 1786. The ferry crossing lies between Augusta and Higginsport, Ohio. Continuing southeast beyond Augusta, KY 8 runs along Dover’s southern edge, then leads upriver toward Maysville.

moments.title: Augusta
moments.text: Confederate Colonel Basil W. Duke attacked Augusta on September 27, 1862, seeking a crossing of the Ohio River. His Second Kentucky Cavalry fought the Bracken County Home Guard in town, where Union defenders sheltered in brick buildings. The Confederates won, but casualties and depleted artillery ammunition made Duke abandon his intended crossing into Ohio. Two Union gunboats had supported the town from the Ohio River before Confederate fire drove them away. Twenty buildings were burned and destroyed. The riverfront’s Water Street Historic District includes houses from the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, alongside later Victorian villas.

moments.title: Augusta Ferry
moments.text: The Augusta ferry service dates to 1797, when John Boude propelled the ferry by hand. Its crossing connects Augusta with Higginsport, Ohio. The Kentucky landing belongs to a town founded as an Ohio River trading post in 1786.

moments.title: Dover
moments.text: KY 8 skirts the southern edge of Dover, a town on the Ohio River’s south bank. Arthur Fox Jr. laid out the town in 1818; a post office followed in 1833, and incorporation came in 1836. Augusta lies seven miles downriver by highway, while the road continues twelve miles upriver to Maysville.
